newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Jordanan bucks trend of more Dutch fuel surcharges.
newsitem.headline: Jordanan bucks trend of more Dutch fuel surcharges.

text.p: Three more major airlines will be introducing fuel surcharges for air cargo lifted from the Netherlands on December 1.
But a major exception to the rule is Royal Jordanian which is one of very few carriers that have not introduced a fuel surcharge from the Netherlands.
A Netherlands-based spokesman for the Jordanian airline said that he does not expect to see any change in this policy before the end of the year.
The trio raising rates are Garuda Indonesia, South African Airways and Varig Brazilian Airways, who were among a dwindling group of carriers that had not introduced charges.
Forwarders and shippers were hoping no additional surcharges would be announced as most others had already been introduced in early to mid-November.
Garuda Indonesia will be sending out letters on Thursday saying a 17 Dutch guilder cents charge will be introduced, a spokesman said.

South African Airways SAA.CN (SAA) will also implement the charge of 17 Dutch guilder cents on December 1, said the carrier's cargo manager, Frits de Bois. SAA introduced a world-wide surcharge on November 15 from its Johannesburg headquarters.
"We were aware of the Dutch shippers and forwarders asking for a delay to the introduction of these charges."
"We gave a month's notice which was a reasonable time to give the forwarders a chance to inform their clients and we consider this a fair way of dealing with the issue," he said.
Varig Brazilian Airways will implement a 10 U.S. cents fuel surcharge on December 1, said the carrier's Dutch cargo manager, Dirk Hazenoot.
Hazenoot said that he had resisted pressure to implement rates any sooner to give the customers a fair amount of notice, -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
